A function that answers a request. It runs on the thread of the connection that sent the request,
one request at a time per connection, and many handlers run at the same time for different
connections (unless the server has only one thread). A handler may block (a slow handler delays only
its own connection) but must protect state that it shares with other handlers.

A body that a function writes to the connection, for content that is not available as a whole
or too large to hold in memory. Whatever the function writes is sent at once. Its length is not
known, so the body is sent in chunks (
) and the connection can be used for
the next request; an HTTP/1.0 client, which does not know chunks, gets the body up to the end of the
connection. If the handler sets a
header, the body is sent with that length instead: the
function has to write exactly that many bytes, or the connection is closed after the response.
